propositions: Parallel multi-session writes cause compaction to mutate the worktree before committing, leaving dirty trees on worker death that block git merge and strand local ticket commits.
Tracked runtime markers (*/.archived, */.write.lock) committed before gitignore rules were added remain as tracked dirt in every status check, preventing push/plan-review attestation.
Reconverge and push recovery must handle both untracked-file collisions and tracked-file deletions/modifications to complete union merge without orphaning commits.
Crash-atomic compaction requires an intent journal outside the worktree to distinguish completed folds from abandoned partial folds, enabling rollback-on-failure recovery.
Store-wide scans (fsck, compact-all) must default to active tickets only and accept --include-archived to reach full store, scaling cost with active working set.
fsck detects dirty-tree and stale-lock classes (tracked deletions, untracked leftovers, orphaned locks) and doctor --repair heals safe cases under write lock.
